summary.headline: Modi Naturals H1 FY27 revenue rose 19.3% to Rs 361.9 crore and EBITDA 25.1% to Rs 40.8 crore, with Q2 margins squeezed by input costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 38.9% YoY to Rs 204.9 crore, with EBITDA up 23.2% to Rs 18.6 crore and margin at 9.1%. Management said input cost increases in edible oil and grain outpaced selling price adjustments in Q2, but early signs of input price normalisation have appeared. Ethanol expanded capacity from 282 KLPD to 600 KLPD and the company cites Rs 494 crore of OMC orders plus a 7.8 lakh KL-type volume order for the next ESY. Management reiterated FY27 guidance, which implies a heavy second half.

segments.name: Consumer division
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 87.4 crore and EBITDA Rs 4.9 crore. Analysts noted revenue has been stuck around Rs 45-50 crore per quarter; management attributes this to lower olive oil prices and stronger food-category distribution.

segments.name: Bulk division
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 80.8 crore and EBITDA Rs 0.7 crore. Q2 revenue was driven by higher realisations; management expects realisations to moderate as commodity prices correct.

segments.name: Ethanol division
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 193.7 crore and EBITDA Rs 34.9 crore. Capacity expanded to 600 KLPD from 282 KLPD, fully operational around August 2026; orders of about Rs 494 crore from OMCs; grain prices weighed on margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: management confident of achieving it; analysts cited about Rs 125-165 crore revenue and Rs 100-105 crore EBITDA with Rs 66-70 crore PAT, implying H2 must be well above H1.
Management expects H2 to be heavier than H1, driven by consumer growth, ramp-up of expanded ethanol capacity and a more favourable input cost environment in bulk.
Long-term sustainable margins: bulk/ethanol 12-15% per management; consumer division 5-8% over the long term.
Consumer raw material costs improved sequentially in Q3; full margin normalisation expected in about one more quarter.

Ethanol: no order slippage; some supply timeline extensions granted. Order for the ESY starting 1 November 2026 (about 7.8 lakh KL volume for cycle 1) implies about Rs 500 crore revenue, about Rs 600 crore including by-products.
capex_capacity: Ethanol capacity expanded from 282 KLPD to 600 KLPD; second facility commissioned and fully operational around August 2026.
Ethanol capacity expansion capex is in the range of a few hundred crore rupees; exact figure to be shared later.
By-products (DDGS) contribute about 18-20% of ethanol division revenue, expected to stay in this range.
Consumer division: new snacking, grocery and high-protein launches (including ready-to-eat popcorn under the Pasta brand) expected over the next two to three months under existing sub-brands.
demand_pricing: Consumer: management says olive oil prices fell, reducing top-line, while food category distribution and availability improved. Rice bran oil costs rose sharply in Q2; company says branded (MRP-driven) oil is a fixed-price business, unlike commodity oil.
Consumer raw material prices reportedly rose about 52% sequentially in Q2 (per analyst question; management did not dispute).

Ethanol: government permits E85 and E100 in flex fuel vehicles; OMC orders growing and private OMCs entering. Analyst noted OMCs cut ethanol prices by about Rs 3 per litre; management said higher fixed-price ethanol share reduces dependence on molasses-linked margins.
Bulk: input costs rose faster than selling price increases in Q2; management sees early signs of input price normalisation.
Consumer brand ambassador: Karishma Kapoor renewed for OLLIN for another year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has consumer business revenue stagnated around Rs 150-180 crore over five years and Rs 45-50 crore per quarter recently? Can volume data be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat top line mainly to olive oil price declines, with growth in food categories and better distribution expected to reflect in coming quarters. Volume disclosure was not committed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 ethanol revenue jump in line with orders, and will Q3-Q4 see slippage?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was fully operational around August; revenue expansion partly in Q2 and fully in Q3. No order slippage; some supply timeline extensions were granted.

qa_highlights.question: Is ethanol-based consumer product launch near?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured permissions for diversification as a hedge; no launch soon, will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 deliver guidance given ethanol price cuts and raw material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, as a higher share of fixed-price ethanol reduces dependence on molasses-linked margins; expects more orders in subsequent tender cycles.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumer margin outlook and when will raw material costs normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer raw material costs improved sequentially in Q3; normalisation may take another quarter. Long-term consumer margin 5-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider a buyback given low valuation and lower short-term debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit; earlier stance was to use cash to repay debt as needed, with the call open in future.

risks_watch: H2 must deliver roughly 1.5x H1 EBITDA to meet guidance of Rs 100-105 crore; any delay in ethanol ramp-up or grain cost relief is a key risk.
Consumer division revenue has been flat at about Rs 45-50 crore per quarter with thin profit (H1 EBITDA Rs 4.9 crore); watch whether new launches lift volumes.
Bulk division profitability is volatile (H1 EBITDA Rs 0.7 crore) and dependent on commodity price swings.
Ethanol pricing pressure from OMC rate cuts and grain-based feedstock shift; cycle 2 and 3 tender wins are unconfirmed.
Ethanol capex and depreciation figures not disclosed; detailed numbers promised later.
summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance and ethanol order book, but cautious on near-term margins; answers were often vague on specifics (capex, tier split, volumes) and deferred details to post-call follow-up.
key_quotes: So we are on track to cover all of it.
We expect cost pressures to ease and business performance to improve over the coming quarters.
But I still think 12 to 15 percent is the long term margin profile.

adds.what: Ethanol capacity expansion from 282 KLPD to 600 KLPD (second facility), fully operational around August 2026

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance (analyst-cited ~Rs 965 crore revenue, implying ~14% growth on the brief's figures, and EBITDA Rs 100-105 crore) without management confirming figures; backing is the commissioned 600 KLPD ethanol capacity and Rs 494 crore OMC orders plus a ~Rs 500 crore ESY order, but H2 must run well above H1 and consumer/bulk recovery remains unproven.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 9.1% (H1 11.3%) as edible oil and grain costs outpaced price hikes; consumer raw material costs improved sequentially in Q3 with normalisation about one more quarter, and management's long-term bulk/ethanol margin is 12-15% and consumer 5-8%, but ethanol prices were cut by about Rs 3/litre by OMCs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (already live, ramp in Q3-Q4 FY27)
rows.why: Ethanol capacity rose from 282 to 600 KLPD (+112.8%), fully operational around August 2026, so the added volume is already in the system and ramps through H2 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 to be heavier than H1 on the ethanol ramp-up, with ESY order of about 7.8 lakh KL implying around Rs 500 crore revenue, but consumer volumes have been flat at Rs 45-50 crore per quarter and no volume disclosure was committed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Ethanol expansion capex is only described as a few hundred crore rupees with exact figure deferred; no utilisation figure was disclosed and no new capex plan was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated FY27 guidance and analysts still need H2 to be about 1.5x H1 EBITDA (Rs 100-105 crore FY target vs Rs 40.8 crore H1), so an upgrade looks unlikely given the margin squeeze and ethanol price cuts.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver roughly 1.5x H1 EBITDA to hit Rs 100-105 crore; risks are ethanol ramp delays, grain cost relief not arriving and OMC price cuts of about Rs 3/litre, though management says there is no order slippage.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Consumer snacking, grocery and high-protein launches, including ready-to-eat popcorn under the Pasta brand, are expected within two to three months under existing sub-brands; an ethanol-based consumer product was said to be far off.

rows.label: ESY order of about 7.8 lakh KL for cycle 1 starting 1 Nov 2026
rows.why: Order implies about Rs 500 crore revenue (about Rs 600 crore including by-products), on top of Rs 494 crore of existing OMC orders, though cycle 2 and 3 tender wins are unconfirmed.

rows.label: Consumer raw material cost normalisation
rows.why: Consumer raw material costs improved sequentially in Q3 and management expects full margin normalisation in about one more quarter, from a Q2 rise of about 52% sequentially per analyst question (not disputed by management).

rows.label: Buyback or faster debt repayment
rows.why: Management declined to commit to a buyback and kept the option to use cash to repay debt as needed, with debt-to-equity at 0.85x as of 30 Sep 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance, the 600 KLPD ethanol ramp and the order book, but cautious on near-term margins and vague on capex, consumer volumes and buyback; analysts pressed on the flat consumer top line, H2 needing about 1.5x H1 EBITDA, and ethanol price cuts.
